text:
mara: quick sanity check before i codify this into an RFC follow-up. idea: a unified continuous-batching fastpath for tiny requests (<= few tokens) that avoids creating lots of tiny queue islands. want to capture tradeoffs and safe defaults.

jon: interesting. immediate risks i see: (1) kv-cache pointer hoarding causing starvation, (2) kernel-launch churn hurting throughput, (3) streaming client semantics when requests get requeued.

mara: agreed. sketching constraints: small-fastpath should be opt-in per tenant, limited concurrency via tokens per-GPU, and a soft-lease that allows preempt/requeue.

peter: prefer soft-lease over hard kill. if runtime can checkpoint kv pointers (cheap), we should pause and resume rather than lose prefix reuse. otherwise requeue as cold with exponential backoff.

rachel: how do we decide which requests are preemptable? naive approach: protect requests with kv_touch_count >= K at admission (set protected bit). cheap to compute at probe time.

john: (typo) jon here: also we need an admission interface separation. scheduler should only give window_hint/deadline and tokens; runtime handles kv decisions and can emit pressure signals back. keep APIs tiny.

mara: proposed minimal API lines: scheduler -> runtime: admit(id, window_hint_ms, priority); runtime -> scheduler: pressure(kernel_launch_rate, kv_eviction_rate); runtime -> scheduler: kv_protect(request_id, reason).

peter: telemetry we need: fastpath_kernel_launch_rate, fastpath_concurrency, kv_touch_histogram, preempt_requeue_count, prefix_reuse_ratio, fastpath_p95/p99, throughput_rps. also a derived metric "fastpath_unit_cost" = extra_launches_per_min * cost_per_launch. product will ask.

rachel: rollout plan: canary with tokens=1 per GPU, synthetic mixed load (short prompts bursts + long tails) for 30-60m. rollback triggers: kernel_launch_rate > baseline*2 AND throughput drop >10%; or prefix_reuse_ratio drop > 15%; or preempt_requeue_count > X.

ops-bot: I can create flags/dashboards. suggested flags: fastpath.unified.canary, fastpath.tokens_per_gpu, fastpath.adaptive_window=true. will add alerts for kernel_launch_rate > 2x baseline (5m) and preempt_requeue_count spike. :robot_face:

mara: control loop idea: runtime returns pressure hints; scheduler reduces tokens if pressure sustained > 2m. keep adjustments conservative (step down 1 token / 5m). add a cooldown. we'll include pseudo-code in RFC.

jon: one more gotcha: streaming clients expecting continuous data may get partial responses if we preempt mid-stream. need a compatibility mode: either disallow fastpath for streaming or guarantee resume semantics (harder). record that tradeoff.

peter: testing note: include end-to-end tests for resume vs requeue behaviors and a scenario where many tenants opt-in simultaneously to see global effects.

rachel: protect heuristic: protected=true if kv_touch_count >= 3 OR estimated_reuse_score > threshold. make threshold conservative initially.

mara: good. i'll draft RFC sections: motivation, safety knobs (tokens, protected bit, soft-lease ms adaptivity), minimal APIs (admit, pressure, kv_protect), telemetry + cost model, rollout playbook, and testing checklist.

jon: i'll review the API sketches and the streaming compatibility section.

peter: i'll take telemetry and cost model.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-8001 for dashboard and INF-8002 for feature flag. :robot_face:

mara: thanks. i'll post the RFC link when it's queued for review.
